source: Per-company annual-report extraction (Claude.ai routine, daily batch of ~10)

china_plus_one.evidence: Cummins India exports to multiple international markets (~17% of revenue); domestic sales grew 18% to ₹8,395 Cr while export grew only 6% to ₹1,771 Cr in FY25. No explicit China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative found in available MD&A — export business is tied to parent Cummins Inc. global supply chain rather than a diversification play.

govt_capex.evidence: Cummins India secured first annual maintenance contract for a large hyperscale data center in FY25; supplies diesel gensets for infrastructure, construction, power generation, and railways. Government capex-linked sectors are significant but exact revenue % not disclosed in available MD&A.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ₹1,771 Cr, ~17% of total FY25 revenue of ₹10,166 Cr. Domestic revenue ₹8,395 Cr grew 18% YoY; export revenue grew 6% YoY.

govt_capex.evidence: CG Power serves state and central utilities, Indian Railways (traction electronics), cement, steel, and textiles industries through Industrial Systems and Power Systems segments. Government-linked power utilities and railway sector are primary demand drivers for transformers, switchgear, motors, and drives. Revenue % from government/infra projects not explicitly disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports contribute approximately 5% of total turnover; company serves customers across 50+ countries in Europe, Americas, Asia Pacific, Africa, and Middle East.

pli_scheme.evidence: CG Power's semiconductor subsidiary CG Semi established India's first ATMP/OSAT facility in Sanand, Gujarat under India Semiconductor Mission. Consortium with Renesas (Japan) and a Thai firm; ₹7,600 Cr total investment. Government subsidy ~50% of project cost. G1 pilot plant capacity: 0.5 million chips/day; G2 facility: 1.45 crore chips/day. Revenue from semiconductor operations not yet material in FY25 (facility commissioned but ramping).

china_plus_one.evidence: Shaily Engineering is explicitly positioned as a China+1 beneficiary in healthcare plastics and drug-delivery devices. Global pharma MNCs are actively diversifying supply chains away from China; Shaily's healthcare segment revenue grew 48–54% YoY in FY25 driven by collaborative design-to-manufacture contracts with MNC pharma companies. GLP-1 drug delivery device orders (obesity/diabetes drugs) represent the leading wave. Healthcare pharma clean-room facility expanded from 44,000 to 127,000 sq ft; injection moulding capacity grew from ~65 to 200+ machines.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue was 77.8% of consolidated revenue in FY2025 (35+ countries, 40+ country footprint); United States is largest single export destination at ~40–45% of exports (~31–35% of total company revenue).

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI scheme capex incentive deadline has passed; company is not a PLI beneficiary. Management stated in earnings calls that PLI scheme is specific to certain components and the investment deadline is no longer applicable to Shaily's product segments.

govt_capex.evidence: Apollo Hospitals signed MOU with Central Government for CGHS Apollo Dialysis Clinics; government healthcare scheme patients (Ayushman Bharat, CGHS) contribute to revenue but % not disclosed. Insurance and cash patients account for 83% of inpatient revenue; insurance revenue +13% YoY, cash patients +15% YoY.

inr_exposure.evidence: International inflows from overseas patients (Middle East, Africa, Indonesia, Iraq, Iran, Sri Lanka) accounted for ~8% of total FY25 consolidated revenue of ₹21,794 Cr. International patient volumes saw 1.5% uptick from Middle East/Africa, partially offsetting 1.5% decline in Bangladeshi patients.

FY2025 total income ₹1,497.3 Cr; FY2026 disclosed geography (USA/NA 35%, Europe 33%, India 24%, ROW 7%) used as structural proxy for FY25 given similar business mix. Neuland serves ~80 countries with 70 US DMFs and 980+ regulatory filings. US/NA revenue is in USD; Europe revenue in EUR. Export pct 76% confirmed directionally from historical data (FY23: ~73% export, trending higher with CMS growth).

govt_capex.evidence: Defence sector contributed 78.5% to total revenue in 9M FY25 (April–December 2024); Q1 FY26 defence share rose to 86%. FY25 full-year defence/govt revenue estimated ~79% of ₹1,051 Cr total revenue (FY25: +15.7% YoY, EBITDA margin 25.6%). Primary customers: DRDO, defence PSUs (BEL, ECIL), Indian armed forces.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (including deemed exports) contributed approximately 12–21% of revenue across quarters in FY25 (Q1FY25 exports 21%; Q1FY26 exports 10%); FY25 full-year export estimated ~18% of ₹1,051 Cr total revenue.

govt_capex.evidence: Polycab supplies cables to infrastructure projects; Railways and Road Transport Ministries maintained near-full budget utilization in FY25, driving demand. W&C segment ₹188,881 million (+18% YoY), representing 84% of total sales. Government infrastructure capex is a key demand driver but exact revenue % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International cables business revenue ₹13,452 million in FY2024-25, contributing 6% to total turnover. Business experienced modest degrowth due to structural and geopolitical challenges in export markets.

Consolidated FY25 revenue ₹1,136 billion; geographic split: India 20%, Europe 38%, North America 25%, China 11%, Others 6%. export_other_pct of 17 = China 11% + Other regions 6%. North America revenue (~25%) primarily in USD; Europe (~38%) primarily in EUR; China (~11%) in CNY. Net profit INR 38 billion in FY25.

pli_scheme.evidence: Motherson Electronic Components Pvt Ltd (MECPL) secured incentives under Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) announced by MeitY for enclosures for consumer electronics industry. Planned ₹1,900 Cr investment over 6-year incentive period (FY26–FY31); manufacturing at Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu with 5,000+ planned jobs. Pre-revenue stage in FY25.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 total revenue from operations ₹49,267 Cr. Export volumes: 1.86M units (+13.9% YoY) out of 4.65M total (40% by volume). Q3 FY25 export revenue ₹4,500 Cr on ~₹12,500 Cr quarterly revenue (~36%); full-year export revenue estimated ~35% accounting for lower realization per exported unit vs domestic premium mix. Key export markets: Africa (Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt), LATAM (Argentina, Mexico, Colombia, Peru — 17% YoY growth), MENA (Egypt, UAE, Saudi Arabia — 29% YoY growth).

pli_scheme.evidence: Bajaj Auto's full portfolio is PLI certified; PLI incentives accrue consistently quarter-after-quarter and are deployed to fund competitive pricing actions in the market. EV portfolio (Chetak, electric three-wheelers) covered under PLI for advanced chemistry cells and auto sector PLI.

china_plus_one.evidence: INOX India secured a significant order from Australia for Oxygen, Nitrogen, and CO2 IMO containers directly competing with Chinese suppliers. User base spans 100+ countries served via after-sales support network in 30+ countries. Q4 FY25 export revenue ₹205 Cr = 53% of Q4 revenue (up sharply YoY). FY25 total revenue ₹1,354 Cr; export ~53% (~₹718 Cr) based on Q4 FY25 export data. Export growth narrative present in quarterly results commentary; no explicit 'China+1' framing found in available MD&A.

govt_capex.evidence: Industrial gases division serves hydrogen/green energy infrastructure and LNG dispensing projects linked to government energy transition plans. Some government-linked capex exposure but revenue % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 total revenue ₹1,354 Cr. Export ~53% of revenue. Industrial Gases division 61% of FY25 revenue (largest); LNG 19%; Cryo Scientific ~20%. Exports to 100+ countries; USD revenue estimated ~40% of total (mix of USD, EUR, and other currencies across global industrial gas markets).

china_plus_one.evidence: Premier Energies is India's second-largest integrated solar cell and module manufacturer (3.2 GW total cell capacity as of FY25). Some international customers prefer India-made solar modules amid tariff/geopolitical pressures on Chinese panels, but the company does not explicitly frame strategy around China+1 in available MD&A summaries. Export share ~4% of FY25 revenue of ₹6,652 Cr (exports <1% in FY26 per latest data).

govt_capex.evidence: Solar modules predominantly sold to government-tendered utility-scale solar projects (SECI, state DISCOMs, PM Kusum, ISTS-linked) and large IPPs. Indian solar capacity additions are predominantly government-funded or government-tendered. Domestic share is ~96% and near-entirety of India market is government/regulated-utility linked. Revenue % from specifically government-tendered projects not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue ₹6,652 Cr (+110% YoY); domestic 96%, export ~4% (~₹266 Cr). Product mix: solar modules 74%, cells 23%, other 3%. 1.2 GW TOPCon solar cell line commissioned in FY25 taking total cell capacity to 3.2 GW.

pli_scheme.evidence: Premier Energies is a confirmed beneficiary of India's Solar PLI scheme (PLI for High Efficiency Solar PV Modules). Manufacturing capacity expansion to 3.2 GW cells linked to PLI commitments. No confirmed PLI tranche received as of Sep 2025; PLI incentives support scale-up with exact PLI incentive income not yet material or separately disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue ₹8,940 Cr (+16% YoY); consolidated net profit ₹738 Cr (+35% YoY). Revenue from outside India ~₹4,898 Cr = 55% of total. Business mix: domestic branded generics ~45% (Zerodol, Revelol, CTD brands); API exports ~20%; regulated market formulation exports (UK, Canada) ~12%; emerging market branded generic exports ~15%; institutional ~8%. USD revenue estimated ~55% of total (API sales to US/EU buyers + branded generics in USD markets + regulated formulations).

china_plus_one.evidence: Aditya Infotech (CP Plus) sources approximately 90% of its surveillance camera components from China (CMOS sensors, SoCs, modules). Despite operating in a segment where Chinese brands (Hikvision, Dahua) face government procurement bans, CP Plus is NOT a China+1 beneficiary — it is heavily China-dependent for manufacturing inputs. Revenue ~99% domestic with <1% exports. FY25 revenue ₹4,221 Cr. The company benefits from India-made branding but its supply chain remains China-centric; any disruption to China component supply would be material.

govt_capex.evidence: CP Plus supplies surveillance systems to government offices, Smart City projects, Indian Railways, police departments, and public safety installations. Government procurement is a meaningful revenue source but specific % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Near-fully domestic business (~99% of revenue from India market). Export share <1% and USD revenue negligible. FY25 revenue ₹4,221 Cr; net profit ₹368 Cr (includes ~₹249 Cr one-time non-cash gain). USD exposure is primarily on the import side (component sourcing from China in USD).

china_plus_one.evidence: RR Kabel exports cables to international markets (~26% of revenue). Western buyers are actively qualifying Indian cable suppliers amid concerns about Chinese cable product quality and supply chain resilience. RR Kabel has been gaining new export customers in the Middle East and Europe in this context. Export growth is consistent with the China+1 qualification wave for Indian cable manufacturers. Annual report FY2024-25 PDF was located but not accessible for direct extraction.

govt_capex.evidence: RR Kabel supplies cables for power transmission, industrial, and residential infrastructure. Government infrastructure capex drives demand for power cables but exact revenue % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Cable insulation materials (PVC, XLPE) are petroleum-derived and crude-linked, alongside copper/aluminium conductors. PVC/XLPE are crude-linked but % of total raw material cost not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~26% of FY25 revenue; FY25 highest-ever ₹9,722 Cr (+27.6% YoY). Wires and Cables segment ~90% of total revenue. Export markets: Middle East, Europe; US exports ~2.5% of total revenue. USD + EUR denominated. USD revenue estimated ~15% of total.

china_plus_one.evidence: Himadri Speciality Chemical is positioning itself as a 'China Plus One global supplier' for advanced battery anode materials (lithium-ion EV batteries). Export revenue ~26.81% of total per Equitymaster analysis of FY25 AR; exports to 61 countries (expanded from 56 in prior year). Anode material business targets global EV battery manufacturers seeking non-Chinese supply. Company approved setting up a subsidiary in China for global expansion — indicating dual-track engagement with China alongside the C+1 positioning narrative.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is coal tar (a by-product of coal/coke at steel plants) — a coal derivative, not crude oil. Coal tar pitch is ~70% of product portfolio; carbon black and specialty chemicals make up the remainder. No significant petroleum/crude-linked raw material exposure.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~26.81% of total per FY25 AR analysis. FY25 revenue ~₹3,800-4,000 Cr (FY26 consolidated ₹4,661 Cr; EBITDA grew from ₹847 Cr FY25 to ₹1,006 Cr FY26). Exports to 61 countries across Asia, Europe, and Americas. USD revenue estimated ~20% of total.

china_plus_one.evidence: Syrma SGS Technology is a leading EMS company benefiting from 'Make in India' and global supply chain diversification from China. Export revenue was ~23% of FY25 revenue. Company cites global electronics supply chain diversification as a growth driver. FY25 revenue ₹3,836 Cr (+19.4% YoY); net profit ₹185 Cr (+48.3% YoY). EMS sector broadly benefits from the China+1 trend as global OEMs qualify Indian manufacturing alternatives.

govt_capex.evidence: Syrma SGS serves defence electronics customers including DRDO-linked programs. Government defence procurement drives a portion of revenue. Specific % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue ₹3,836 Cr. Export revenue ~23% of revenue, primarily to US and European customers under global EMS contracts. USD revenue estimated ~15% of total.

pli_scheme.evidence: Syrma SGS received PLI (Production Linked Incentive) approval for the MedTech business, enabling expansion in healthcare electronics manufacturing. Company also benefits from SPECS scheme for electronics. PLI-linked revenue is in early stages and not yet material in FY25.

china_plus_one.evidence: Elgi Equipments is the 6th largest air compressor manufacturer globally and 2nd largest in India. Exports ~46% of consolidated revenue through subsidiaries in Americas, Europe, Australia. Competes with Chinese compressor brands in global markets. No explicit China+1 narrative found; the company's international strategy pre-dates the China+1 trend.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue ₹3,510 Cr; India standalone ₹1,899 Cr (54%); international subsidiaries ₹1,611 Cr (~46%). Americas, Europe, Australia subsidiaries generate local-currency revenue. Americas (USD) estimated ~15-18% of consolidated revenue; Europe (EUR) ~15%; Australia (AUD) ~6-8%. USD revenue estimated ~15% of consolidated. In FY26, consolidated grew to ₹3,951 Cr (+13%).

rural.evidence: Thangamayil Jewellery operates primarily in Tamil Nadu with strong presence in tier-2/tier-3 towns and semi-urban markets. ICRA notes 'long presence and strong brand recall in Tamil Nadu.' Plans to open eight mid-level retail outlets across Tamil Nadu targeting semi-urban customers. Specific rural revenue % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: 100% domestic jewellery retailer operating in Tamil Nadu. No export or international revenue. Revenue driven by gold price appreciation and volume. FY25 operating income grew ~16–18% YoY.

rural.evidence: Marico has a large rural distribution network for Parachute coconut oil, Saffola, and Nihar brands, particularly strong in rural Bengal, Odisha, and South India. Rural distribution is a strategic priority cited in annual reports but specific rural revenue % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Marico's own risk disclosure states: 'direct exposure to volatile crude derivatives is limited to about 18–20% of its total raw material base.' Primary crude-linked inputs are HDPE packaging and specialty wax/polymer additives. Main inputs — copra and vegetable oils — are not crude-derived.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved hedging policy; translation risk unhedged
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue ₹10,831 Cr (+12% YoY; first time crossing ₹10,000 Cr). Q4 FY25: India ₹2,068 Cr (76%); International ₹662 Cr (24%). Full-year India ~76%, International ~24% (~₹2,600 Cr). International: Bangladesh (largest single international market, BDT), Middle East (AED/USD ~5%), Africa (USD), South-East Asia (VND/MYR ~3%), USA (~2%). Constant currency international growth 14% in FY25. USD revenue estimated ~10% of total (Middle East + partial Africa).

govt_capex.evidence: NMDC is a Navratna PSU under Ministry of Steel (100% GoI owned) and India's single largest iron ore producer (~25–30% domestic market share). Iron ore sold to domestic steel producers including PSUs (SAIL) and private players (Tata Steel, JSW Steel, JSPL). Demand is driven by domestic steel sector capex and production growth. H1 FY26 turnover ₹12,895 Cr, PAT ₹3,663 Cr. Q2 FY26 production 10.21 MT, sales 10.72 MT.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: All revenue in INR from domestic sales
inr_exposure.evidence: NMDC sells all iron ore domestically to Indian steel manufacturers — 100% INR-denominated revenue. Sixth-largest iron ore producer globally but no meaningful export revenue. FY25 annual revenue estimated ~₹22,000–24,000 Cr based on quarterly run rates.

govt_capex.evidence: Defence sector contributed approximately 18% of consolidated FY2025 revenue (up from 9% in FY2024), driven by Pinaka Multi-Barrel Rocket Launcher System (MLRS), Nagastra-I loitering munitions, 155mm artillery shells, and UAV/anti-drone systems under Indian government defence contracts. Industrial explosives (72% of FY25 revenue) also serve government infrastructure and mining projects. Highest-ever order book of ~₹21,000 Cr of which ~₹18,000 Cr is from defence.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/overseas explosives revenue crossed ₹1,000 Cr in FY25; export defence orders of ₹1,076 Cr booked. FY25 total revenue estimated ~₹7,100 Cr. Export ~14% of consolidated revenue. International explosives sales to mining markets in Africa, Middle East, and SE Asia; defence exports in USD. Revenue CAGR ~30% over FY2021–FY2025.

pli_scheme.evidence: Solar Industries is a confirmed beneficiary of the Defence PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme under Ministry of Defence. Company manufactures defence explosives, Pinaka rockets, loitering munitions, and ammunition under defence PLI. PLI incentives support indigenisation of defence manufacturing under Atmanirbhar Bharat.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Vijaya Diagnostic Centre is explicitly debt-free (zero long-term debt). Net cash company as of FY25. Floating rate liability percentage is 0% — company carries no interest-bearing debt.

inr_exposure.evidence: Vijaya Diagnostic Centre is a pure-play domestic diagnostics chain (pathology + radiology) operating in South India (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, NCR). FY25 revenue ₹680 Cr (+24.4% YoY; organic growth 18.9%). Revenue is 100% from domestic patients; >95% B2C (direct cash + insurance). No international or export revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: Shriram Pistons exports to 45+ countries across 5 continents (17% of FY25 revenue). No explicit China+1 narrative; primary focus is on OEM supply to domestic auto manufacturers (52%) and aftermarket (26%). Export split: Europe 5.3%, US 1.7%, Asia ex-China 2.2%, Other 7.8% of total revenue.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue ₹3,550 Cr (+15% YoY). Revenue mix: OEM 52%, Aftermarket 26%, Export 17%, Non-automotive 5%. Domestic total 83%; exports 17% to 45+ countries. Export: US 1.7%, Europe 5.3%, Asia ex-China 2.2%, Other 7.8%. 9 manufacturing units and 5 assembly plants. USD revenue estimated ~10% of total (US + Middle East portion of Other). Net income ₹507 Cr (+14% YoY).

pli_scheme.evidence: Shriram Pistons explicitly did NOT join the Auto Components PLI scheme. Company confirmed non-participation in available disclosures.

china_plus_one.evidence: Laurus Labs is a major API manufacturer competing directly with Chinese API suppliers globally; world's leading third-party supplier of antiretroviral APIs (serving Africa and global health programs). CDMO business grew 49% YoY in FY25 as global pharma innovators diversify manufacturing from China. Indian API manufacturers structurally benefit from supply chain diversification. FY25 revenue ₹5,554 Cr (+10% YoY); EBITDA margin 20.1%.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue ₹5,554 Cr; exports ~60% of total. Segment mix: API (ARVs, oncology, cardiovascular) ~37%; FDF/Generics (US regulated + emerging markets) ~35%; CDMO (synthesis for global innovators) ~28%. Export: US 18%, Europe 16%, Other/Africa 26%. USD revenue estimated ~35% of total (US generics + Africa ARVs in USD + global CDMO contracts). 110+ active CDMO projects; 70 US DMFs filed; approved by USFDA, EMA, WHO, TGA.

pli_scheme.evidence: Laurus Labs is a confirmed PLI Bulk Drugs beneficiary under the PLI scheme for Key Starting Materials (KSMs), Drug Intermediates (DIs), and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). The scheme supports domestic manufacturing of critical pharma raw materials to reduce import dependence on China.

govt_capex.evidence: Welspun Corp supplies large-diameter pipes to domestic oil & gas pipeline projects (ONGC, GAIL, HPCL city gas distribution expansion). Government-linked domestic pipeline capex is a key revenue driver, % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is hot rolled coils (HRC, steel) — not crude-linked. Minor crude-linked coating materials (coal tar epoxy, PE coating).

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue ₹13,978 Cr. India operations revenue ₹9,340 Cr (67%); International (outside India, primarily USA subsidiary) ₹4,638 Cr (33%). USA subsidiary ~25% of total revenue (USD-denominated); Middle East/other exports ~8%. Order book ₹19,553 Cr as of March 2025. Welspun USA bagged two orders for US natural gas/NGL pipelines ~USD 715 million. USD revenue estimated ~30% of total. EBITDA ₹1,858 Cr (record); PAT ₹1,908 Cr (+72% YoY).

govt_capex.evidence: KEI Industries supplies cables to government infrastructure projects: urban/rural electrification, solar power projects, highways/tunnelling, railway and metro projects, and refinery expansion. Government infra capex is a significant demand driver. Strategic decision to scale down EPC while growing institutional W&C segment. Revenue % from government projects not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Cables use PVC/XLPE insulation (petroleum-derived) alongside copper/aluminium conductors. PVC/XLPE are crude-linked; specific % of total RM cost not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue ₹9,736 Cr (+20% YoY). Segment: cables 64%, house wires 30%, EPC 4%, SS wires 2%. Export ~13% of revenue (~₹1,266 Cr), primarily Middle East (USD). Company has net foreign currency receivables (exports > FX imports) for last 4 consecutive fiscals FY2022–FY2025 per ICRA. USD revenue estimated ~10% of total.

china_plus_one.evidence: Apar Industries is the world's largest aluminium and alloy conductor manufacturer. Export revenue 32.8% of FY25 consolidated revenue of ₹18,581 Cr (all-time high, +15% YoY). Apar FY24 AR quotes 'Western interest in diversifying supply chain away from China' as a demand tailwind for Indian conductor exports. Global utilities are qualifying Indian manufacturers as alternative to Chinese suppliers. Apar benefits from this trend as a world-class Indian conductor exporter. Domestic revenue grew 40.9% YoY in FY25.

govt_capex.evidence: Apar's conductors power transmission and distribution infrastructure; state and central utilities are primary buyers domestically. Transformer oil serves Indian power utilities. Significant exposure to government-linked power T&D capex but exact revenue % from government projects not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Apar's specialty oils/lubricants segment (transformer oil, industrial lubricants, auto lubricants) contributes approximately 25.7% of consolidated FY25 revenue; base oil (crude-derived) is the primary input for this segment, making its gross margins crude-price-sensitive. Conductors (48% of revenue, aluminium/alloy-based) and cables (27%, copper/PVC) have partial but smaller crude-linked RM exposure.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue ₹18,581 Cr (highest-ever). Export revenue 32.8% = ₹6,095 Cr. Business: conductors 48%, specialty oils 25.7%, cables ~26%. Export markets: USA, Middle East, Africa (conductors); SE Asia (specialty oils). USD revenue estimated ~22% of total (Middle East + partial USA conductor exports + specialty oil exports to USD markets).
